entry.evidence: However, the relative importance of see-level rise and influx of warmer CDW for driving EAIS retreat remains uncertain.

steps.action: Pose the open question of which forcing, sea-level rise or warmer CDW inflow, drove post-LGM EAIS retreat, and note the lack of field records of past ice-surface change.
steps.quote: the relative importance of see-level rise and influx of warmer CDW for driving EAIS retreat remains uncertain

steps.action: Take the two rival triggers from the literature: warm CDW inflow causing ice-shelf melt and collapse, and sea-level rise from Northern Hemisphere deglaciation.
steps.quote: Another potential trigger for perimeter-wide ice sheet retreat is sea-level rise19,20.

steps.action: Survey three nunataks in Gjelsvikfjella, select stable, minimally weathered erratics (Methods), and measure in situ 10Be and 26Al on 39 quartz-bearing erratics by AMS.
steps.quote: We measured in situ 10Be and 26Al concentrations on 39 quartz-bearing erratics collected from Gjelsvikfjella

steps.action: Correct sample nuclide concentrations for background measured in procedural blanks and normalize AMS ratios to standards (Methods only).
steps.quote: Concentrations reported in Supplementary Data 2 involved subtraction of background 10Be and 26Al atoms measured in procedural blanks.

steps.action: Use 26Al ages to check correspondence with 10Be ages, to screen for inherited nuclides, and to validate nuclide quantification (Methods and supplement).
steps.quote: Exposure ages from 26Al were only used to check their correspondence to 10Be-based exposure ages (within error ranges)

steps.action: Convert 10Be concentrations to exposure ages (CRONUS-Earth V3, LSDn scaling), plot them against height above the ice reference surface, treat older ages as recycled outliers, and reconstruct the Grjotfjellet ice-surface history: an LGM highstand at moraine I, ~100 m above present at ~8.4 ka, ~15 m at ~5.7 ka.
steps.quote: the ice sheet surface was ~100 m higher than at present at ~8.4 ka, but rapidly thinned down

steps.action: Replicate the thinning history at a second nunatak, Rabben: ~70 m above the reference surface at ~8.2 ka, thinning to ~20 m by ~6.5 ka, with R09 treated as a recycled clast.
steps.quote: This dataset shows a strikingly similar trend to that from Grjotfjellet

steps.action: Infer from Terningskarvet ages of 774 to 2460 ka that the summit was probably not covered by ice at the LGM.
steps.quote: it is likely, but not certain, that the LGM glacial highstand remained below the summits in Terningskarvet

steps.action: Run 75 high-resolution Úa steady-state LGM experiments for the Jutulstraumen catchment across basal sliding, rheology and CMIP5/6 climate forcing, and retain 53 that meet observational criteria, to test whether local sites reflect regional change.
steps.quote: A total of 75 experiments spanning a range of plausible basal sliding, rheological, and climate conditions

steps.action: Compare modeled LGM elevation differences with the field inferences: 80–205 m at Grjotfjellet, 120–250 m at Rabben (consistent with >70 m), and 30–50 m lower than present at Terningskarvet (consistent with an ice-free summit).
steps.quote: In those preferred models, the ice sheet is 120–250 m higher than at present at Rabben

steps.action: Keep the claim that Grjotfjellet and Rabben represent the sign, but not the magnitude, of coastal-sector thinning below the escarpment hinge zone.
steps.quote: Grjotfjellet and Rabben, by virtue of their location downstream of the escarpment, are representative of the regional coastal sector ice-sheet changes

steps.action: Set the record against other DML LGM thickness constraints and the Sôya Coast chronology ~1400 km away, and use a large-scale EAIS model to show that the inland-to-coast thinning gradient is common to all DML catchments.
steps.quote: A study of the post-LGM deglaciation in the easternmost area of DML depicts a strikingly similar story to ours31.

steps.action: Estimate thinning rates and onset ages by Monte Carlo linear regression (iceTEA, 5000 iterations): 0.05 m/yr with onset 8.3 ka at Gjelsvikfjella, and 0.15 m/yr with onset 8.6 ka from reanalysed Sôya Coast data.
steps.quote: the composite best-fit thinning rate for the sites in Gjelsvikfjella is 0.05 m yr−1

steps.action: Compare the rates and onsets with other Antarctic sectors, and argue that the synchronous onset at two distant sites implies a common external forcing.
steps.quote: the consistent timing of thinning onset at two sites that are ~1400 km apart could demonstrate synchronized ice-sheet thinning

steps.action: Use coupled atmosphere-ocean GCM ocean temperatures at 450 m (CDW depth) offshore DML from the co-authors' earlier simulations (Obase et al. 2021).
steps.quote: A coupled atmosphere-ocean general circulation model shows that the ocean temperature at a water depth of 450 m

steps.action: Compare the thinning onset with MWP-1A, ice-core atmospheric temperatures (Dome Fuji, EDML) and modeled ocean warming: thinning began 2000–4000 years after the warming.
steps.quote: our documented thinning of the EAIS in DML was initiated 2000–4000 years later, indicating the presence of another controlling process

steps.action: Exclude CDW warming (and MWP-1A) as the sole immediate trigger of the rapid thinning because both clearly preceded it.
steps.quote: clearly preceded the initiation of the rapid ice-sheet thinning

steps.action: Hypothesize that a regional relative sea-level highstand, set by global sea-level rise and delayed GIA uplift, triggered the rapid thinning.
steps.quote: [...] propose regional sea-level rise, determined by global sea level and regional GIA, as a trigger of rapid EAIS thinning in DML.

steps.action: Compute GIA regional sea level at the Jutulstraumen grounding line with the original ICE6G ice-load history across a range of mantle viscosities: a broad peak at 8–9 ka.
steps.quote: find that sea level exhibits a broad peak at 8–9 ka

steps.action: Compare ICE6G deglaciation histories with the field chronologies at Grjotfjellet, Rabben and Sôya Coast: magnitudes agree, but the ICE6G onset is ~2000 years too early.
steps.quote: the initiation of thinning at ~11 ka in the ICE6G model clearly predates the onset of thinning constrained by field evidence by ~2000 years

steps.action: Refine the ICE6G ice-load history for drainage systems 5–7 by delaying the onset of thinning from ~11 to 9 ka, with magnitude unchanged and linear thinning to present by 5 ka.
steps.quote: [...] the regional sea-level change based on a refined ICE6G ice-load model

steps.action: Recompute regional sea level with the refined load: a clearer highstand of at most 30 m at 9–7 ka, caused by delayed viscoelastic uplift.
steps.quote: The refined regional sea-level history exhibits a clear highstand of at most 30 m above current sea level at 9–7 ka

steps.action: Test sensitivity with three other refinements (delay to 10 ka; refinement applied to all drainage systems; both) and with the mantle-viscosity range (Methods and supplement).
steps.quote: We found that the results are consistent among all refined models

steps.action: Compare the refined highstand with the onset of thinning and find that they coincide, concluding that the highstand paced the EAIS response.
steps.quote: A more pronounced regional sea-level highstand that coincides with the initiation of rapid ice-sheet thinning indicates that this process played a key role

steps.action: Refine the mechanism into two stages: CDW reached the ice front by ~11 ka and caused limited coastal retreat; sea-level rise to 9–8 ka then allowed CDW beneath the ice shelves, grounding-line retreat via marine ice sheet instability, and thinning >100 km inland.
steps.quote: The sustained sea-level rise likely promoted grounding-line retreat by increased ice-shelf buoyancy and facilitated warm CDW inflow beneath the ice shelves

steps.action: Support the interpretation with a published Lazarev Sea marine sediment record showing fully marine conditions in the Early Holocene.
steps.quote: This interpretation is supported by a marine sediment record recovered from the Lazarev Sea

steps.action: Extend the hypothesis: Mid-to-Late Holocene GIA-driven sea-level fall stabilized the ice shelves, pinned on ice rises, and may have caused the readvance recorded by moraine IV.
steps.quote: likely stabilized ice shelves and reduced calving

steps.action: Support the readvance with published Riiser-Larsen marine sediments and Sôya Coast shell-bearing lacustrine sediments, and note similar readvances in other sectors.
steps.quote: The notion of a readvance is supported by marine sediments recovered offshore of the Riiser-Larsen Ice Shelf

steps.action: Keep the claim that abrupt Early-to-Middle Holocene regional deglaciation of coastal DML was probably triggered by a regional sea-level highstand with prior CDW warming as a prerequisite, and state that it needs future testing.
steps.quote: This event was probably due to a regional sea-level highstand that facilitated the inflow of warmer CDW.

tree.answer: Nature repeats across Grjotfjellet, Rabben and Sôya Coast ~1400 km away
Highstand robust to refinement variants and mantle viscosity; site representativeness supported by 75-run ensemble
Sea-level highstand with prior CDW warming kept as best explanation; CDW alone rejected as immediate trigger

end.claim: Abrupt regional-scale thinning of the EAIS [...] DML from the Early to Middle Holocene was probably triggered by a regional relative sea-level highstand that facilitated warm CDW inflow beneath ice shelves, with prior CDW warming as a prerequisite.

decisive_move.sentence: The exposure-age reconstruction of thinning onset at ~8.4 ka, replicated at Rabben, is what shows that the thinning postdates CDW warming and that the ICE6G timing is too early; without it there is no refined highstand and no claim.

gates.evidence: The 2015–16 field campaign was designed to reconstruct past ice-surface elevation (§2 ¶1; §4.1 ¶1); the sea-level hypothesis is introduced only in the Discussion (§3 ¶6). The CDW-only rival faced a timing test it failed (§3 ¶5). The sea-level hypothesis was tested by coincidence of the highstand with thinning onset, but the refined ice-load model was fitted to the same field chronology (§4.5 ¶2), so the test is only partly independent. Nothing is reported as fixed before the data.

imports.item: Accelerator mass spectrometry of 10Be/9Be and 26Al/27Al normalized to KNSTD standards
ICP-MS and ICP-OES measurement of stable 27Al
Monte Carlo linear regression (5000 iterations) for thinning rate and onset

novelty_claims.quote: [...] , we present a new, well-constrained ice-sheet thinning history for the period since the LGM for Dronning Maud Land
New 10Be exposure ages from Grjotfjellet and Rabben in Gjelsvikfjella provide clear evidence for ~100 m of rapid EAIS thinning between 8.4 and 5.7 ka

limits: No review file, open discussion or earlier version was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. The supplement (Notes 1–5, Supplementary Data) was not supplied; checks reported there (26Al–10Be correspondence, refinement sensitivity, ensemble histograms) are coded from the main-text descriptions only. Inference: the refined ICE6G load is delayed to fit the field chronology, and the highstand is then shown to coincide with thinning onset, so the coincidence is partly built in; the paper does not report a test that could have separated the sea-level trigger from other delayed processes. Snow shielding is assumed negligible and GIA-driven production-rate changes are ignored, with no effect reported. The interval between ~5.7 ka and moraine IV was not sampled. Basal and rheological properties are not constrained by the ensemble. The ocean-temperature simulation is the co-authors' earlier work (inherited). The Sôya Coast data are from Kawamata et al. 2020, which includes a co-author, reanalysed here. Sub-claims and their statuses: thinning rate 0.05 m/yr (0.03–0.10) with onset 8.3 ka (7.6–9.1), estimate_with_resolution; Gjelsvikfjella sites representative of the coastal sector's sign of change, best_explanation from the model ensemble; Terningskarvet ice-free at the LGM, 'likely, but not certain'; Late Holocene readvance, explicitly 'needs to be further verified'; synchronized thinning across DML, stated as 'could demonstrate'. The authors state that the mechanism must be tested by future studies.
